inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for Q2 2026 (4,062m; Q2 2026 results, note 'Weighted average number of shares - diluted'). 4,007m shares in free issue at 30 June 2026 plus ~50m dilutive awards. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the GBP2bn buyback completed June 2026 with no successor programme announced (Nuvalent financing takes priority).
inputs.net_debt_note: GSK-defined Total net debt at 30 June 2026 GBP15,132m (gross debt 18,238 incl. lease liabilities, cash and liquid investments 3,106), LESS lease liabilities estimated at ~GBP700m (830m at 31 Dec 2025 less 106m H1 repayments and 136m Rockville disposal, plus new leases; treatment B below), PLUS the Nuvalent acquisition (closed 15 July 2026, after the balance sheet date): ~$9.4bn net of acquired cash at $1.35/GBP = ~GBP6,960m, debt-funded. Pro forma ex-lease net debt = 15,132 - 700 + 6,960 = 21,392. Q3 2026 results (due late Oct 2026) will show the actual post-Nuvalent figure and should replace this estimate.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, share-based incentive plans add-back GBP374m (Metrics CSV StockBasedComp). No separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis); UK filer, awards largely cash-settled/withheld within the charge.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income GBP169m FY2025 NOT stripped: GSK is a GBP21bn net-debt company, so there is no cash pile being double-counted. The component build starts from core operating profit, which excludes finance income anyway.
inputs.last_fcf_note: reported_fcf (CSV FreeCashFlow 6,393 = OCF 7,741 - PP&E capex 1,348) is BEFORE purchases of intangibles (1,637), and AFTER the Zantac settlement cash (1,195), ViiV/Shionogi contingent-consideration payments (1,330, inside operating activities) and net finance costs paid. last_fcf = 6,393 - 374 = 6,019 per the house identity, but it is not the forward anchor: the forward build is from components (core operating profit basis) with the contingent consideration and restructuring cash carried in the equity bridge and intangibles purchases charged inside capex_pct. Normalised FY2025 unlevered owner FCF after NCI leakage on that basis is ~GBP6.4-6.7bn (GSK's own FCF 4,029 + net finance 525 + Zantac 1,195 + CC payments 1,330 = 7,079, less the ~550 gap between cash tax paid 1,202 and a normal 18% charge, less the 182 gap between NCI distributions and NCI profit share).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury shares GBP1,377m; H1 2026 GBP634m completing the GBP2bn programme (June 2026). Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (flat count, SBC expensed).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to the quote in pence. No FX risk in the conversion itself (same currency, unit change); parity check: GSK NYSE ADR (GSK, 1 ADS = 2 ordinary shares) trades at ~2 x 17.50 x USD/GBP. The underlying cash flows are ~50% USD / ~26% EUR, so the GBP flows carry translation exposure: management's own sensitivity is -2pp on 2026 sterling turnover growth and -4pp on core operating profit growth at July 2026 rates ($1.35/GBP).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the flows' currency: 10y gilt ~4.5%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~0.6 for a large diversified pharma -> cost of equity ~7.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (3.7% after tax); pro forma weights ~76% equity (GBP71bn market cap) / 24% debt (GBP21bn net debt) -> blended ~6.6%. Rounded UP to 7.0% as a modest buffer for the GBP-reported/USD-earned translation mismatch. Same WACC in all three scenarios: dolutegravir LoE, pipeline attrition and US pricing risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path charges principal (GBP241m FY2025 'Repayment of lease liabilities') plus lease interest (~GBP40m est. on ~GBP0.8bn liabilities) = ~0.9% of revenue inside EBIT; lease liabilities (~GBP700m at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net_debt; da_pct_path is core D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (depreciation 2,314 - ROU depreciation 206 + core amortisation 450 [total 1,258 - 808 acquired-intangible amortisation excluded from core] = 2,558 = 7.8% of FY2025 revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: ViiV Healthcare NCI (Pfizer ~11.7%, Shionogi ~10%): profit attributable to NCI GBP573m FY2025 (distributions 391), guided 'unchanged' for 2026. Charged ONCE, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined leakage rate on model EBIT = cash tax ~18% (core tax rate 17.1% FY2025, guided ~17.5% 2026, Pillar Two drift to ~19%) + NCI ~6.5% of EBIT (573 / ~8.8bn). The combined rate eases from 24.5% to 23.5% from 2030 as dolutegravir LoE shrinks ViiV's (and therefore the NCI's) profit share faster than the tax rate rises. No NCI stock deducted in the bridge (balance-sheet NCI is only GBP515m and would understate it anyway).
inputs.contingent_consideration_treatment: Model EBITDA is built from CORE operating profit, which excludes the ViiV/Shionogi (and Novartis Vaccines, Affinivax) contingent consideration remeasurement and the GBP1.3bn/yr cash payments (which GSK reports inside OPERATING cash flow). The flows therefore exclude these payments; the liability is deducted in the equity bridge instead: GBP6,781m at 30 June 2026 (Q2 2026 note, CCL at end of period), net of tax at 18% because GSK confirms the payments are tax-deductible = GBP5,560m. The liability's own discount rate (~9% Shionogi) is above the 7% WACC, so the fair value is if anything a conservative proxy.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, Drivers route (make build-dcf). GSK is a large-cap global biopharma operating company with no bank/REIT/LIC characteristics, so the owner-FCF engine is the correct route; non-US adaptations applied: GBP WACC, GBp quote (fx_rate 100), leases treatment B, NCI as leakage in the flows, contingent consideration and restructuring cash in the equity bridge. FY0 = FY2025 (last full year); year 1 = FY2026, ~75% elapsed at valuation (end-of-year discounting of FY2026 is slightly conservative). Base revenue is CONTINUING operations post-Haleon (demerged July 2022): FY2018-21 revenue of ~GBP34bn included Consumer Healthcare and must not be extrapolated. FY2022 reported net income includes a GBP7.65bn demerger remeasurement gain (kpis NetProfitAttributable 14,956); the 4,461 continuing figure is used. EBITDA margin anchor: FY2025 core operating profit 9,783 (29.9%) less lease interest, plus SBC 374, lease cost 281 and core D&A ex-ROU 2,558 = 12,956 = 39.7% of revenue; FY2026 guided core margin >31% CER (~30.7% AER after the sterling headwind) -> 40.2%. Capex_pct 9.0% = PP&E 1,348 (4.1%) + purchases of intangibles 1,637 (5.0%): intangibles purchases are recurring licensing/milestone reinvestment for a pharma that in-licenses pipeline (GBP1.0-1.8bn every year since 2019) and are charged as capex, per the parser's flag. Bolt-on M&A (RAPT GBP2.1bn H1 2026, Nuvalent GBP7.0bn July 2026, IDRx/Boston Pharma 2025) is NOT charged as a recurring flow: Nuvalent is carried at cost in net debt and its pipeline (zidesamtinib/neladalkib, launches 2027-28) is in the base growth path from 2029; future deals are assumed value-neutral at fair value. Working capital capture -10% of the revenue change (receivables + inventory exceed payables; growth consumes cash). Pension deficit and residual Zantac exposure (~GBP0.3bn of the $2.2bn settlement unpaid) are small relative to a GBP71bn market cap and are not bridged. Price is the 9 Oct 2026 LSE regular close (not after-hours).

equity_bridge.item: ViiV/Shionogi and other contingent consideration liabilities, after tax (6,781 x (1-0.18))
equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 results: CCL at 30 June 2026 GBP6,781m (current 1,376 + non-current 5,405); cash payments ~GBP1.3bn/yr sit in operating cash flow but outside core operating profit, so they are excluded from the flows and the liability is deducted here. Tax-deductible per FY2025 AR p.98.

equity_bridge.item: Accelerate Growth restructuring cash cost, after tax (2,100 x (1-0.18))
equity_bridge.note: Programme announced 28 July 2026: GBP2.4bn total cost, GBP2.1bn cash, majority charged 2026-2027; savings of GBP1.9bn p.a. by 2029 are what hold the core margin flat through dolutegravir LoE in the base path, so the cost is charged here and the benefit in the margin path.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (continuing operations FY2022-FY2025, 3.7%) cross-checked against the 2031 outlook (>GBP40bn risk-adjusted CER = ~3.4% CAGR from FY2025)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 15.6% diverges >30% from revenue (3.7%) and EPS (8.3%): shareholders' equity was cut to GBP10.6bn by the July 2022 Haleon distribution and has rebuilt since, so the equity CAGR is a balance-sheet artefact, not earnings power. All 5yr CAGRs span the demerger (FY2020 includes Consumer Healthcare) and are shown for completeness only.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped for a net-debt company): FY2020 6,834 -> FY2022 5,145 -> FY2025 6,019. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (5.4%) is in line with reported (5.2%): SBC is flat at ~1.1% of revenue, so none of the growth is being paid for in stock. Note reported FCF here is before intangibles purchases and after Zantac/contingent-consideration cash, so the level is noisy year to year even though the trend is sound.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3.0% sterling (guidance 3-5% CER at the upper half, ~-2pp FX; H1 2026 AER +3.5%). FY2027 +4% on the Specialty launch cycle (Exdensur, Blenrep, Blujepa, Penmenvy, LAI HIV). FY2028-30 +3/+1.5/+1.5% as dolutegravir loses US exclusivity from April 2028 and EU mid-2029 (~GBP5bn+ franchise, majority of impact 2029-30 per management). FY2031 +3.5% as Nuvalent oncology (launches 2027-28), bepirovirsen and the 20+ phase III starts contribute; FY2031 revenue GBP38.4bn vs the >GBP40bn CER outlook (~GBP38.8bn at today's sterling), i.e. the base sits ~1% under management's risk-adjusted number. Fade to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Core operating margin 29.9% FY2025, guided >31% CER for 2026 (~30.7% AER) and 'broadly stable' through the LoE window, underwritten by GBP1.9bn of Accelerate Growth savings by 2029. Model EBITDA = core-margin-equivalent + SBC 1.1 + lease 0.9 + D&A 7.8: 40.2% in FY2026 rising to 40.6%, dipping to 40.0% in FY2030 at the trough of dolutegravir erosion, recovering to 40.5%. Cash tax + NCI leakage 24.5% easing to 23.5% post-LoE.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.0% nominal growth and a 15x owner-FCF cap: a mature pharma with a perpetual LoE cycle; Gordon at 7%/2% would be 20.4x, so the cap binds. The market pays ~12.5x pro forma EV / normalised unlevered FCF today, so 15x assumes some re-rating once the dolutegravir cliff is visibly absorbed.

bull.rationale: FY2031 revenue GBP41.7bn: the >GBP40bn outlook delivered in sterling plus Nuvalent upside; LAI HIV (Cabenuva/Apretude, already 35% of US HIV) offsets most of the dolutegravir cliff so FY2029-30 still grow 3%; Shingrix ex-US immunisation (12% vs 45% US) keeps vaccines growing; Accelerate Growth savings drop through to a 32-33% core margin. 16x cap, 2.5% terminal growth.

bear.rationale: Dolutegravir erodes like a classic small-molecule cliff (revenue -4% in each of FY2029 and FY2030, ~GBP3.5bn lost) with LAI cannibalisation rather than offset; General Medicines keeps shrinking 5-7%/yr; Arexvy loses to Abrysvo/mRESVIA and Shingrix US demand plateaus; two or three of the 2026 phase III starts fail (camlipixant precedent); MFN pricing extends beyond the three-year tariff deal. Core margin falls to ~27% (model EBITDA 36%) as the Accelerate Growth savings are absorbed by R&D and price. 12x cap, 1.5% terminal growth; FY2035 revenue GBP32.8bn, flat on FY2025 in nominal terms.

scenario_narratives.base: GSK executes roughly to its own plan but at today's sterling: Specialty Medicines (HIV LAIs, Nucala/Exdensur, Blenrep, Jemperli, Ojjaara) grows low double digits, Vaccines are flat to slightly up, General Medicines shrinks mid-single digits. The dolutegravir loss of exclusivity (US April 2028, EU mid-2029) knocks group growth to ~1.5% in FY2029-30 while the Accelerate Growth savings hold the core margin broadly flat at ~31%, exactly as guided. FY2031 revenue GBP38.4bn, ~1% below the >GBP40bn risk-adjusted CER outlook translated at current rates. Nuvalent's ROS1/ALK assets and the 20+ phase III starts lift growth back to 3.5% in FY2031-32 before fading to 2.5%. The GBP6.8bn Shionogi contingent-consideration liability and GBP2.1bn restructuring cash are paid from the flows via the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: The HIV long-acting injectable franchise (Cabenuva, Apretude; 80% of HIV growth in Q2 2026) grows fast enough that ViiV holds revenue through the dolutegravir cliff; Shingrix ex-US penetration climbs from 12% toward US levels; Blenrep, Exdensur and Blujepa launches hit consensus peaks; Nuvalent's zidesamtinib and neladalkib add GBP1-2bn by 2031; and the GBP1.9bn cost programme drops through, taking the core margin to 32-33%. FY2031 revenue GBP41.7bn, above the outlook. The market re-rates a 9x forward P/E pharma toward peers (16x FCF cap).
scenario_narratives.bear: The patent cliff is the story: dolutegravir-based sales (~GBP5.4bn annualised) halve across FY2028-30 and LAIs cannibalise rather than add; General Medicines continues its -7 to -9% decline under Medicare Part D redesign; Arexvy keeps losing RSV share and Shingrix plateaus; a run of binary phase III readouts fail as camlipixant did (GBP1.3bn impairment, July 2026); MFN pricing concessions persist after the Section 232 tariff relief lapses in January 2029 and a stronger pound compounds it. Revenue falls 4% a year in FY2029-30 and only recovers to FY2025's level by FY2035; the core margin slips to ~27% as R&D is protected. The Nuvalent GBP7bn and RAPT GBP2.1bn purchases, already in net debt, deliver little. 12x FCF cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the 15/50/35 default to 30/50/20. Bear up: the dolutegravir loss of exclusivity is a dated, certain event (US April 2028) affecting a ~GBP5bn+ franchise and the question is only the slope of erosion; the July 2026 camlipixant failure shows the late-stage pipeline the 2031 outlook relies on is genuinely binary; US MFN pricing terms are not fully public; and GSK has a decade-long record of under-delivering on outlooks. Bull down: it needs the LAI offset, the Shingrix ex-US ramp, three or four launches at consensus peak AND the restructuring savings all to land independently. Base keeps 50%: ~90% of the 2031 outlook is from products already approved or launching within three years, and 2026 guidance was narrowed to the upper half in July.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a core-operating-profit component build, SBC expensed and the count held flat, leases as an operating cost, ViiV minority leakage inside the tax/leakage rate, and the two large non-core cash claims (Shionogi contingent consideration GBP6.8bn, Accelerate Growth restructuring GBP2.1bn) deducted after tax in the equity bridge rather than hidden in a margin. Purchases of intangibles are charged as recurring capex because GSK in-licenses its pipeline every year. Net debt is pro forma for the July 2026 Nuvalent acquisition. The valuation is deliberately anchored at or slightly below management's 2031 outlook in the base case and lets the dolutegravir cliff and pipeline binaries play out through the bear weighting, not through an inflated discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Slope of dolutegravir erosion from April 2028 (US) and mid-2029 (EU): every GBP1bn of lost high-margin HIV sales not replaced is roughly GBP0.5bn of owner FCF, ~10% of the FY2030 flow
Binary late-stage pipeline outcomes behind the >GBP40bn 2031 outlook (camlipixant failed July 2026; 20+ phase III starts in 2026 are unproven)
US drug-pricing policy: MFN agreement terms and what follows the Section 232 tariff exemption after 20 January 2029
Sterling: ~50% USD / ~26% EUR revenue in a GBP model; a 5% stronger pound is ~-4% on GBP revenue and more on margin
Net debt anchor is an estimate pending Q3 2026 results: lease liabilities (~GBP700m) and the Nuvalent net cash cost (~GBP7.0bn at $1.35) should be replaced with the reported 30 September 2026 figure
Terminal cap of 15x owner FCF in the base case versus a market currently paying ~12.5x: part of the base-case upside is a re-rating that the market may never grant a company with a visible LoE cycle
Recurring bolt-on M&A (GBP4.4bn 2025, GBP9bn+ 2026 incl. Nuvalent) is assumed value-neutral; a history of paying above value for pipeline would make capex_pct understate true reinvestment
